pharm: Human urinary trypsin inhibitor (glycoprotein) that inhibits multiple serine proteases and modulates inflammation.
quick: Acute pancreatitis: 100,000 units IV infusion 1-3 times daily
Safety not established; use only if clearly needed
Infusion reactions, vital signs, underlying condition
summary: Ulinastatin is a human urinary trypsin inhibitor (a glycoprotein protease inhibitor) used parenterally in several Asian countries for acute pancreatitis, acute circulatory failure/shock, and as an adjunct in sepsis and major surgery. It inhibits trypsin and other serine proteases and has anti-inflammatory effects on neutrophils and cytokines. It is NOT FDA-approved; the dosing and indications below derive from manufacturer prescribing information and clinical use in Japan/India/China. Evidence is heterogeneous and it should be used per local regulatory approval and protocols.
indications: Acute pancreatitis (including acute exacerbation of chronic pancreatitis)
Adjunctive management of sepsis and systemic inflammatory response (per regional approval)
Adjunct during major/cardiac surgery to attenuate inflammatory response (regional use)

dosage.n: Dissolve in 500 mL of 5% glucose or normal saline; infuse over 1-2 hours
May give 100,000 units in 10 mL saline as slow IV push over ~5 minutes; adjust to severity
Per local protocol; dose/duration vary by study

admin: For intravenous use only; reconstitute/dilute in 5% dextrose or 0.9% saline
Infuse over 1-2 hours, or give slow IV bolus for the smaller volume preparation
Use freshly prepared solution; do not mix with other drugs in the same infusion
Administer in a setting able to manage hypersensitivity/anaphylactoid reactions
moa: Glycoprotein urinary trypsin inhibitor that inhibits a broad range of serine proteases (trypsin, chymotrypsin, elastase, plasmin, hyaluronidase) and stabilizes lysosomal membranes; it suppresses neutrophil activation and pro-inflammatory cytokine release, attenuating tissue injury in pancreatitis and systemic inflammation.
preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established; use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: Safety during breastfeeding has not been established; use with caution.
renal: No specific dose adjustment established; limited pharmacokinetic data in renal impairment.

moderate: Gabexate mesilate and other protease inhibitors - do not mix in the same line (precipitation/instability)
interactions.diagnostics: Limited interaction data; do not co-administer in the same infusion with other agents.

monitoring: Signs of hypersensitivity during and after infusion
Liver enzymes and blood counts with repeated use
Response of the underlying condition (pancreatic enzymes, hemodynamics)
counsel: This medicine is given by a drip or injection into a vein in hospital
Tell staff immediately if you feel itching, rash, flushing, or difficulty breathing
It is used to calm inflammation in conditions like pancreatitis or shock
Report any discomfort at the infusion site
pk: Store as per manufacturer; use prepared solution promptly
pearls: Not FDA-approved; used in Japan, India, China, and other countries - dosing here follows regional manufacturer prescribing information and is not from a US/openFDA label
Human urinary trypsin inhibitor with broad anti-protease and anti-inflammatory action
Evidence in sepsis/pancreatitis is mixed - use as an adjunct within approved indications and local protocols
Watch for anaphylactoid reactions during infusion
missed: Administered in hospital on a scheduled basis; a delayed dose is given as soon as feasible and the schedule resumed by the clinical team. Patients do not self-administer.
overdose: Specific overdose data are limited. There is no specific antidote; manage supportively, monitor for hypersensitivity and hemodynamic effects, and provide symptomatic care.
